AO.label: Backlog growing with no escalation threshold
AO.observation: The work order backlog has grown over the twelve-month period and ACSA has defined no threshold at which a backlog item is escalated.

AO.label: Corrective work dominates the mix
AO.observation: Corrective work orders substantially exceed preventive work orders over the period, indicating a reactive maintenance regime.

AO.observation: Work orders were closed in Oracle eAM without hours worked and feedback recorded as D060 016M cl. 4.3 requires.

IO.label: No ACSA PM compliance or backlog target
IO.finding: No ACSA document states a PM compliance percentage, a backlog ageing limit or a corrective to preventive ratio target, so maintenance performance cannot be scored against an ACSA threshold and the absence is itself the finding.

IO.label: PM completion below the 90% benchmark
IO.finding: Planned preventive maintenance completion over the twelve-month period is below the 90% benchmark, so assets are running beyond their scheduled maintenance intervals.

IO.label: Work orders exceed the 7 or 14 day rule
IO.finding: Issued work orders were not executed within the fourteen days or seven days of issuance stated in D060 016M cl. 4.2.1 and remain open beyond that period.

IO.label: Ageing backlog of very old open orders
IO.finding: A substantial volume of work orders has been open for more than ninety days with no closure plan, so deferred maintenance is accumulating unmanaged.

IO.label: Overdue actions not reported on variance report
IO.finding: Actions overdue by seven days or more with no completion date are not being reported on the System Variance Report as required by Z001 001M cl. 4.11.

IO.label: No follow-up work orders from findings
IO.finding: Findings noted on completed work orders do not generate follow-up work orders as required by D060 016M cl. 4.3, so defects identified during maintenance are not tracked to closure.

IO.label: PM closed without evidence of work done
IO.finding: Preventive maintenance work orders were closed as complete with no service tag, logbook entry or signed hard copy evidencing that the work was carried out at the asset.

IO.finding: The fire watch was not held for at least thirty minutes after completion of hot work, the work area was not inspected one hour after completion and the site was not periodically monitored for a further three hours, contrary to S010 002WI cl. 4.3.3 and 6.2.7.

IO.label: Gas test results not recorded on the permit
IO.finding: Gas testing results were not recorded on the face of the hot work permit form as required by S010 002WI.

IO.label: Electrical work without M&E 070 and ME 069
IO.finding: Work on electrical apparatus or in a live chamber was carried out without a Permit to Work M&E 070, a Risk Assessment ME 069 and a Workers Register ME 068 as required by D060 011M cl. 4.3.

IO.label: Two different combustible clearance distances
IO.finding: S010 002WI states a combustible clearance of thirty-five feet at cl. 4.2 and 4.5 but ten metres at cl. 4.3.3 for the same control, and S010 003M cl. 4.3.4.7 compounds this by stating 'five (10) meters', so KSIA teams may be applying different separation distances for the same hot work.

IO.label: Permit retention rules contradict each other
IO.finding: D060 011M cl. 4.6 requires original work permit forms and completed permit books to be retained twelve months before destruction while its own section 11 records table sets five years for the Permit to Work ME 070 and the permit books, and cl. 4.25 sets the contractor audit at a prescribed or contracted frequency while section 6.2 states monthly.

IO.label: Confined space procedure outside the document set
IO.finding: The Confined Spaces Entry Procedure S010 007M is cross-referenced by S010 002WI cl. 4.6, D060 021M cl. 4.6.2 and D060 012M but is not in the 99-document set, so the confined space limb of the permit system cannot be evidenced.

AO.label: SWPs not approved by both appointees
AO.observation: Safe Work Procedures were produced but are not signed by both the GMR 2(1) and GMR 2(7) appointees as required by S010 003WI cl. 4.

AO.label: LPG installation present, no certificate held
AO.observation: An LPG installation is present on site but no Certificate of Conformity was produced and ACSA confirmed no such requirement exists in its procedures.

IO.label: No current hazardous chemical inventory
IO.finding: No current inventory of hazardous chemical substances and dangerous goods classified to SANS 10228 is kept for the site as required by T050 003M cl. 4.1.

IO.label: SDS not accessible at the point of use
IO.finding: Safety Data Sheets are not kept accessible and within close proximity to the hazardous chemical substances in use, contrary to T050 003M cl. 4.1.

IO.label: Flammables stored outside a flammable store
IO.finding: Flammable substances are stored outside a flammable store designed to the National Building Regulations SANS 10400 when not in use, contrary to T050 003M cl. 4.3.

IO.label: Incompatible substances stored together
IO.finding: Incompatible substances, including oxidisers stored with flammables, are held together in the same store with no segregation.

IO.label: Statutory registers missing or not retained
IO.finding: The Register of Dangerous Goods EMS 109, Hazardous Substance Register EMS 102, Asbestos Register EMS 103 or Transformer and Substation Register EMS 104 was not produced or is not retained for the period set in T050 003M cl. 11.

IO.label: SWPs unapproved without a GMR 2(7) appointee
IO.finding: S010 003WI cl. 4 requires every Safe Work Procedure to be approved by both the GMR 2(1) and GMR 2(7) appointees, so if no GMR 2(7) has been appointed at KSIA every Safe Work Procedure at the airport is technically unapproved.

IO.label: No ACSA LPG, segregation or ventilation requirement
IO.finding: ACSA states no LPG installation certification requirement, no storage segregation requirement or incompatible-materials matrix, and no ventilation requirement or air-change rate for chemical or flammable stores anywhere in the document set, so those limbs of this check cannot be assessed against a stated ACSA standard.

IO.finding: Gas cylinders are stored unsecured and are able to fall, presenting a valve-shear and uncontrolled-release hazard.

IO.finding: Oxygen cylinders are stored with flammable gas cylinders with no segregation, creating a fire and explosion hazard at a designated Major Hazard Installation.

IO.finding: The gas cylinder storage area is neither ventilated nor marked with warning signage identifying the gases held.

IO.finding: Pressure equipment has not received the statutory three-yearly inspection and test required by D080 017M cl. 4.2.3 and the Pressure Equipment Regulations register has not been updated.

IO.label: SCBA cylinder below 80% of filling pressure
IO.finding: An SCBA cylinder was found below 80% of the recommended filling pressure or outside the four-yearly hydrostatic test interval set by S010 004M cl. 4.9.

IO.finding: No written Safe Work Procedure for compressed gas cylinders and handling of cylinders, approved by both the GMR 2(1) and GMR 2(7) appointees, was produced as required by S010 003WI.

IO.label: ACSA states no cylinder storage requirements
IO.finding: No ACSA document in the 99-document set requires cylinders to be stored upright, secured, segregated by gas type, ventilated, signed, or full and empty cylinders to be separated, the only cylinder-specific figures ACSA states being 300 bar, 80% of filling pressure and a four-yearly hydrostatic test for ARFFS breathing apparatus in a PPE procedure, so this check must be assessed against SANS 10087-1 and SANS 10019 in the absence of an ACSA standard.
